question.problem: What is the value of $x$ given that $a=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ x\end{aligned}]$ and $a⊥b?$
question.worked_solution:
We know that $a⊥b$ ($a$ and $b$ are perpendicular) if and only if $a\cdot b=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =2x\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 4+5\cdot x \\  & =-6x-4+5x \\  & =-x-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ -x-4 & =0 \\ x & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
